newsitem.title: FRANCE: CYCLING-TRAVERSONI TAKES STAGE AFTER THREE RELEGATED.
newsitem.headline: CYCLING-TRAVERSONI TAKES STAGE AFTER THREE RELEGATED.

text.p: Italian Mario Traversoni won the 19th stage of the Tour de France on Friday despite crossing the line 26 seconds behind the first two riders home.
Dutchman Bart Voskamp and Jens Heppner of Germany were relegated and fined by the race jury for infringements.
Voskamp and Heppner cut across each other's line over the final metres in a frantic two-man sprint to the finish line of the 172-km stage from Montbeliard.
"It was found that on two occasions the two riders in the lead did not hold their line in the final sprint," a statement by the race jury said.
It said Voskamp, who crossed the line first, and Heppner had been fined 200 Swiss francs each and relegated to 10th and 11th respectively in the stage placings.
Another rider, Belgian Peter van Petegem, was also fined the same amount and relegated to 12th "for irregular sprinting".
Traversoni came in at the head of 12 riders, who with Heppner and Voskamp had formed a breakaway group very early in the stage.
"When I came out of doping control and was told both front riders could be disqualified and I could get the win I didn't believe it," Traversoni said.
"My objective in the Tour was to get on the sprinters' podium. These points will help."
The race jury took some time coming to a decision, announcing it shortly after the peloton, including overall leader Jan Ullrich, came in nearly 18 minutes behind.
Both Heppner and Voskamp were shocked by the decision.
"I think I sprinted well. A sprint's a sprint," the Dutchman said.

"I deviated two centimetres from my line and they take my win away. After the finish I was sure I had won. It's unbelievable, these poor people who make the Tour a laughing stock," he said of the jury.
Heppner said: "For me the jury's quite crazy. It's not normal that the decison should go to a rider 20 to 30 seconds behind."
Voskamp and Heppner staged their two-man break from the leading 14-man group some 30 kms from the finish of the flat stage, last before the final two stages in the Paris area over the weekend.
Earlier, the group had opened a gap of nearly 10 minutes over the peloton after about 95 kms.
On Saturday Ullrich could increase his lead of six minutes 22 seconds if he dominates the Disneyland time trial as he did the St Etienne one last Friday.
Ullrich, on course to be crowned Tour winner on the Champs Elysees on Sunday, has shown signs of fatigue over the last few stages but he is in a class of his own in time trials.
